deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a laboratory record from Gauss's absolute determination of the horizontal magnetic intensity (the experiments of 1832 behind 'Intensitas vis magneticae terrestris ad mensuram absolutam revocata'). The next page is headed 'May 2'. The moment of inertia K of the suspended needle is found by fixing the same pair of weights (total mass m) at different distances r from the suspension axis. The oscillation period t is then measured, using t^2 proportional to (K + m r^2). The previous page gave the run with r = 177.45, where t ≈ 20.27 s. This page gives the runs with r = 231.4 and r = 20.0 mm.

(A) r = 231.4. Passage times are recorded for oscillations n = 0, 1, 4, 5, 6, 52–55 and 90–92, from 4h28'30.72 to 5h2'13.46. Gauss 'reduces with 22.00': he subtracts n·22.00 s from each time.
- Reduced seconds: n=0: 30.72; 1: 30.72; 4: 30.76; 5: 30.76; 6: 30.68; 52: 30.24; 53: 30.26; 54: 30.24; 55: 30.18; 90: 29.54; 91: 29.54; 92: 29.46 (the last three after the minute shift).
- Group means: n=0½: 30.720; n=5: 30.733; n=53½: 30.230; n=91: 29.513.
- Corrected period: t = 22 + (29.513 − 30.720)/(91 − 0.5) = 22 − 0.013337 = 21.98666, written 21.9867. This is the endpoint slope; the inner groups serve as control.
- The side table lists scale readings at n = 0, 57, 58, 94–97. Their exact role cannot be fixed from the page; they are presumably for the amplitude ('nicht unendlich kleine Schwingung') correction p^2 T/21887500 set up on the previous page. That correction is not explicitly applied here.

(B) r = 20.0 mm. Times for n = 0–3, 76–79 and 149–151, from 5h13'18.04 to 5h57'23.66. These are reduced with 17.52 s, i.e. Gauss subtracts n·17.52 from each time.
- Reduced seconds (13' + …): 18.04, 18.06, 18.12, 18.10 | 18.32, 18.25, 18.29, 18.32 | 18.16, 18.10, 18.14.
- Group means: n=1½: 18.080; n=77½: 18.295; n=150: 18.133.
- Periods: 17.52 + 0.215/76 = 17.5228; 17.52 − 0.162/72.5 = 17.5178; 17.52 + 0.053/148.5 = 17.5204 (adopted).

(C) Implicit use (mine). From T1²(K + m r2²) = T2²(K + m r1²):
K = m (T1² r2² − T2² r1²)/(T2² − T1²).
With T1 = 17.5204, r1 = 20 and T2 = 21.9867, r2 = 231.4 this gives K ≈ 92 060·m (mm²). Interpolation then predicts t(177.45) ≈ 20.25 s, against the observed ≈ 20.26–20.29. The three runs are consistent.

(D) Results noted at the bottom:
- 'Statisches Moment 15149, log = 4.18037'. Probably the product M·T (magnetic moment times horizontal intensity) or a related static quantity; its derivation is not on the page.
- 'Allein dann folgt' ('but then it follows'): log moment of inertia 9.65344, i.e. 4502·10^6, for the unreinforced needle, and 9.66011, i.e. 4572·10^6, for the reinforced needle. Units are presumably mg·mm².
- Rough apportionment: about 3000·10^6 from the needle alone and 1000·10^6 from the mirror holder ('Spiegelträger').
- If K = 4.502·10^9 mg·mm², then m ≈ 4.9·10^4 mg ≈ 49 g. This inference is mine.
errors: The reduced times in run (A) are labelled 5h28'..., but the raw times start at 4h28'30.72. The label should be 4h (a clock/hour-label slip without numerical effect). Similarly, run (B) raw times are 5h13' but the reduced column is labelled 6h13'.
In run (B), entry n=149 reads 56'40.64 with a digit overwritten. Only 56'48.64 reproduces the reduced value 13'18.16 that Gauss uses, so 48.64 is the correct reading.

The three partial periods of run (B), 17.5228 and 17.5178, differ by 0.005 s, presumably an amplitude effect. Gauss adopts the overall value 17.5204 without explicit amplitude correction on this page.
Otherwise all reductions, means and periods check exactly.

results.what: Reduction of transit times by subtracting n times a trial period, averaging groups, and correcting the period from the drift of group means
results.modern_name: linear fit of transit times / method of coincidences for oscillation period
results.usually_credited_to: standard astronomical/pendulum practice; Gauss's magnetometer procedure (1832)

results.what: Moment of inertia of magnetic needle from periods with the same added weights at different distances: K = m(T1^2 r2^2 - T2^2 r1^2)/(T2^2 - T1^2)
results.modern_name: Gauss's method for moment of inertia (added-mass method) in absolute intensity measurement
results.usually_credited_to: C. F. Gauss, Intensitas vis magneticae terrestris (1832/33)

results.what: Numerical values: log moment of inertia 9.65344 (unreinforced) and 9.66011 (reinforced needle), static moment 15149
results.modern_name: experimental data for absolute geomagnetic intensity determination

deep.surprise_reason: Raw experimental record of Gauss's well-known 1832 absolute intensity measurements (moment-of-inertia determination by displaced weights). The method and context are published and famously his; the page is routine data reduction.

transcription_corrections: '5 30 733' is the group mean 30.733 for n=5 (reduced column labelled 5h28' by Gauss, though logically 4h28').
Entry n=149 should be 56'48.64 (written with an overwritten digit; machine reading 40.64 is inconsistent with the reduction 18.16).
The '17.52' above the r=20 table is the trial period used for reduction (final digit 2 overwritten), not a time.
Reduced value at 1½ is 6h13'18.080 (written with overwritten '80').
'von der Nadel allein ist es pp.' — 'pp.' here means approximately (circa).
